draft: Tier A draft by the fix owner, written before tools/bench.mjs landed. Counts are predicted from the code, not measured by the runner. The bench-author calibrates and proves each check discriminates.
evidence: README 'Before / after' (mobile 6x n=3, old tools: fps 63.7 -> 69.5, frames >20 ms 115 -> 91, disjoint) and 'Visual / behaviour parity' (exit values equal to 3 decimals)

hero.why: Exit progress 0 to past 1 over .hero-track (200vh). Start after the desktop entrance (about 1.8 s, class is-ring-splash-done on .hero): the JS path runs until then on purpose.

exitOpacityWrites.why: Baseline s (JS 4163) writes --exit-opacity on .hero once per engine frame. Patched CSS mode writes none (it removes the property once in d).

heroPointerEventsWrites.why: Baseline s writes style.pointerEvents every frame. Patched writes it only when the IntersectionObserver flips (track bottom crosses 1.05 viewport heights).

cueFloatAnimations.why: On phones the patched cue exit runs as scroll-driven animations on .scroll-float (opacity, translate, filter). The baseline only has the idle bob (transform) there.

exitAnimatedProps.why: Architecture review (webkit.md 1): scroll-driven keyframes only on threaded properties, no custom properties (FINDINGS P3).

mechanism.why: Phones enter CSS mode at mount. Predicted baseline about 10 writes (about 10 steps of 100 px over 932 px of progress, at least 1 write per step).
Desktop enters CSS mode after the entrance (d). The segment starts after it.
Patched: at most one write per IntersectionObserver flip (one near the end, one more if the scroll comes back).
Proves the CSS path is live (supported and attached). If it isn't, the JS fallback runs and the exitOpacityWrites check fails too.

mechanism.patched: contains none of --exit-opacity, --exit-scatter, --copy-in, --entered, width, height, top, left, margin-*, clip-path
mechanism.why: A compliance guard, not a discriminating check: a later edit must not move the exit back to custom properties or layout properties.

parity.why: The cue's opacity and blur move from .scroll-cue to .scroll-float on phones, so compare the product in the visual check, not per element here.

gain.why: Whole-page A/B showed the gain in per-frame style/paint (frames >20 ms, fps), not LoAF. The iPhone check (device iphone) is pending: the phone is disconnected.

experiments.variant: v1: keyframes use animated custom properties
experiments.why: Rebuilt from the session transcript. The breakage (cue stuck at opacity 0) is Safari-only (P3): confirm it with device iphone. Chrome parity may pass.

experiments.variant: v2 with the original local names
experiments.why: Parity: all mechanism and parity checks pass, the same as 04.
The fix. All mechanism checks pass, and styleLayoutMs is lower in the gain scenario.
Visual change on purpose (no exit blur). Mechanism checks pass except cue-exit-is-a-scroll-animation-mobile (no filter). The gain against 04 is unmeasured.

experiments.variant: unregister the hero dE callback in CSS mode
experiments.why: no patch kept: rejected at design time, never built. Predicted: .hero-track loses data-start-selling-scene and data-start-selling-render (P12).
